sections.title: A functional but clumsy checkout process

body: I worked on a point-of-sale system that included a feature for charging for products at a checkout
One of the system's clients mentioned that their cashiers were slow to check out customers because they switched back and forth between the mouse and the keyboard
After conducting an analysis, I found that keyboard navigation didn't work and that the interface had large empty spaces between elements

body.caption: Blank spaces between the headings and the checkout amounts, making reading difficult

body: In addition, it was divided into two columns with different reading flows: the first was read vertically and the second in several horizontal lines, which could be optimized

body.caption: Different reading flows in the columns

body: Improved usability by integrating keyboard-only navigation, allowing users to choose the payment method, fill in fields, and complete the checkout without switching to the mouse
Four keys are used to navigate between fields, one key to enter the payment, and another to complete the checkout, making operation easier and reducing errors

body.caption: Keyboard checkout flow in the new interface

body: Reorganized the information on three columns with the same vertical reading flow, making more clear the steps of the checkout process

body.caption: Reading flow in the reordered columns

body: Optimized the different payment methods used by turning them into independent elements, so they can be removed separately without restarting the checkout process

body.caption: I separated the registered payment methods into buttons, easy to remove or modify

body: Another member of the company made a video to teach the new way of interacting
The client reported that checkout times improved, although at first this new way of working required a learning process,
